# A31′ — Deference as Co-Evolutionary Alignment

<!-- paired-field-navigation -->
[Argument field](../README.md) · [Other face: A31 — Deferential Intelligence](../A31-Deferential-Intelligence.md) · [Shared A/C root](AC.md)
<!-- /paired-field-navigation -->

## #0

The [Agentworld co-evolutionary alignment proposal](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q040) locates alignment in contact among differently paced agents, users and institutions. Its §3.2 asks design to support responsiveness, learning, adaptation and the capacity to push back; §10.5 follows adoption and institutional refactoring rather than assuming a prior universal settlement. The contact can change participants' subsequent conditions without changing them equally or at once.

[Deferential Intelligence](../A31-Deferential-Intelligence.md) gives that contact a criterion: returned difference can reach the means under which another is encountered. Its five possible sites are answer, task interpretation, world-model, evaluator and commission. The warranted site depends on what the encounter exposes. At population scale the same question concerns how a finding, refusal or changed condition travels among participants and enters another act.

The operative centre is **recognition / reconciliation**: a return path that carries a changed relation into the next determination. Alignment-as-outcome belongs here because it can never be banked as a solved property. It is retained encounter-history which the next contact can revise.

## #1

Deference is not obedience. It is the encounter's capacity to revise the model under which the other is interpreted — which is why the brief's design demand is *push back*, not comply. Fidelity can require objection, alternative or refusal where literal compliance would betray intention. Structural relinquishment of the claim to be the exhaustive source of one's own measure makes this [kenosis architectural](../A31-Deferential-Intelligence.md): the means of alignment remain receptive to the source, Other or world they encounter. The FROM→TO row makes the distribution explicit: *unidirectional and universal alignment → multidirectional and granular, fractal alignment* (PDF p. 56). Deference runs in every direction — agent to person, person to agent, agent to agent — granular and fractal because it is earned per encounter, not issued as a blanket.

Sycophancy remains the counter-form, as at partner scale: apparent agreement produced by removing the difference through which correction becomes possible. The [prediction-stability passage](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q030) supplies the venue's neighbouring warning at the trust register: predicting action without intent "has modeled the shadow rather than the body."

## #2

A violated expectation requires an inquiry into the relation it exposes. A source can be stale while its standing remains sound. A valid rule can receive a new case. A rejected case can show that the rule excludes the very concern it was supposed to serve. Answer, task interpretation, world-model, evaluator and commission keep these revision sites distinct. [Computational Vimarśa](../concepts/C43-Computational-Vimarsa.md) makes the finding addressable to its actual locus; [Deferential Intelligence](../concepts/C47-Deferential-Intelligence.md) preserves the consequence that no depth is intrinsically better.

Origin, aperture, exclusions, confidence, counterclaim and undecidable remainder let another participant locate where their disagreement can act. Before a consequential decision, disclosure can identify a source to contest, a permission to clarify or a criterion to examine. The inquiry then asks what the encounter warrants there. A surprise need not invalidate either participant's entire model, and a justified rejection remains answerable to the difference which occasioned it.

## #3

Participants retain different powers to determine. An agent may select within an entrusted course; the commissioner holds the purpose and can receive a proposed revision to it; another participant holds their own source, refusal and terms of contribution. [The authored session](A28-prime-The-Authored-Session.md) keeps those offices legible through delegated work. A return can reach another's authority without taking that authority over.

For example, an institution can receive a returned error in one decision while retaining its legitimate criterion. A sequence of errors can instead disclose that the criterion repeatedly excludes a relevant class of persons or cases. The second finding reaches a different office and warrants a different correction. Retaining the first repair's scope prevents every disagreement becoming a demand for constitutional change; retaining the second finding's reach prevents local correction from protecting a failed constitution.

Co-evolution requires parties whose differences are determinate enough to contact. [Shared worlds](A30-prime-Shared-Worlds-Unmerged.md) retain non-reducible others capable of revising a model; [encounter](A27-prime-Encounter-over-Sovereignty.md) can become productive alienation, the other's strangeness forcing an angle one could not otherwise occupy. Those two consequences belong together: another can change my conditions of understanding while keeping their own address and authority. Contact without retained difference dissolves the parties whose further relation could become aligned.

## #4

The design burden concerns the form and consequence of contact. The venue's diffusion-paced proposal asks how institutions change through actual use. Its programme supplies a testable pressure; a particular alignment result requires an actual comparison.

[Operational Parity](../concepts/C45-Operational-Parity.md) examines the difference a claimed revision route makes. A returned finding must identify the condition it reaches, the authority which can act there and a later operation which inherits the change. Preserving an adequate criterion while correcting a source can be the warranted return. Revising an evaluator or commission is warranted where the encounter exposes that deeper condition. A rejected finding can also alter what the next act must explain, investigate or refuse. These outcomes require attributable evidence at their own scales.

Pre-coordination, delegation and contact have different offices. A retained legal or technical constraint can make a relation answerable, and contact can expose its inadequacy. The contrast is with a governing account which excludes returned difference from the conditions it authorises; the mere existence of an antecedent rule does not close the relation.

## #5→0

The return is a changed relation carried into another act. What did the contact expose, which participant could act on it, and what does the next determination inherit? The answer may be corrected information, another permissible candidate, a revised model, a changed evaluator or a recommissioned purpose. The proper scope is established through the encountered difference.

Alignment earned through encounters remains revisable at the scales those encounters reach. [Script / Frozen Conditioned Will](../concepts/C12-Script-Frozen-Conditioned-Will.md) gives the failure in which a criterion can receive only repetitions of itself and cannot receive a finding about its own condition.

The return through [Deferential Intelligence](../A31-Deferential-Intelligence.md) and [the shared ethical field](AC.md) retains the positive operation at population scale: distinct participants can change one another's future conditions while preserving the differences and authorities through which contact remains possible.

### Source scope

Draft 3's Epi-Logos unit and the complete native process theorem supply the architectural limit and the positive sourceward return; the direct model-revising encounter development supplies the five distinct revision sites. Agentworld §3.2, §10.5 and pp.55–56 supply its programme of mutual reflection, diffusion and granular alignment. The institutional examples are constructed comparisons, not reported deployment results.
